notes:
### New

- New things live in the dark. Rats nest about the catacombs and come for noise and light. Small spiders bite only when you bother them, though some maps have a giant one that hunts, and every bite poisons you and slows you for a minute. Moths gather round a bright lamp left on. Shapes crouch in corners and walk off when they're seen, but one in five is a witch.
- Witches are drawn in by your party's noise and light. Lamps on bright, running, fighting and looting all add up, and when it's too much one turns up a few metres away and comes to look. Go dark and keep still to stay unnoticed. Witches won't follow you into a crawl, a squeeze or the water.
- The surveyor: a friendly mapmaker who wanders the lower levels. Hold E (X on a controller) on him to copy his map into yours.
- The Gloaming is a harder fight. It hunts smarter, charges you down, vanishes and comes back somewhere else, and fires a dark ray that snuffs the lamp it hits. Only weapons wear it down now. The chapel has been rebuilt, three times the size, with a balcony over the door, and its door stays sealed until the Gloaming is banished.
- A new start: the Angel's Well, a candlelit chapel over a pit. One rope goes down, and there's no climbing back up it. Each of you starts in your own spot.
- Jump with Space (A on a controller).
- A crowbar. A quarter of crates are jammed, so try one and pry it open with a crowbar in hand: hold E for 10 seconds, and it's loud.
- False walls. Some dead ends are not what they seem. With a crowbar, hold E on the wall for 5 seconds: a false one comes down, and solid rock does nothing.
- Locked trunks on the third level hold at least one epic or legendary find. Each one's key is hidden in a crate somewhere on the map, and it only has to be in your pack.
- Ledge halls: a tall passage you climb up out of.
- Throw a knife or brick: hold attack to draw it back, and let go once it clicks. A tap still stabs.
- Bandages, medkits and batteries can be used on a teammate: with one in hand, stand still near them and hold right click (LT).
- You see what your teammates hold in their hands, and see them use it and flinch when they're hit. Their gamer tags float above them, hidden by rock. You can turn tags off in Settings > Interface.
- Alerts slide in at the side of the screen for friend requests, party invites and items you receive.

### Changes

- The map is a tab in the menu underground, beside Pack and Rite. M opens it, and it opens on the level you're on. You make scratching sounds as you sketch.
- The Pendant always lies on the chapel's altar, at the angel's feet.
- Taking things from a crate or a body makes noise nearby.
- Squeezes grunt once as you start through and gasp as you come out.
- No way back out at the start: the first way out is the rope at the end of the first level.
- The headlamp: hold F for less than half a second to switch between low and bright. The low beam is dimmer and the bright beam is wider.
- G and D-pad down no longer drop what's in your hand. Drop things from the pack's item menu.
- Esc closes the pack, the map or any open screen before it opens settings.
- New players start in fullscreen.
- The item menu shows Sell and the price.

### Fixes

- The corpses of fallen explorers are life-sized.
- Looking up from under the water shows the surface, not the passage above.
- A stray drag or double-click no longer highlights the HUD.
